title: Keynote: The AI developer experience doesn't have to suck – why and how we built Modal
talk_summary: Modal's CEO explains how they built custom container infrastructure (content-addressed storage, lazy loading, CPU memory snapshots on gVisor) to achieve sub-second cold starts, enabling fast feedback loops and serverless GPU utilization. The core lesson is that fast container startup and usage-based pooling drive both developer productivity and cost efficiency.

takeaways.technique: Content-addressed image storage with dedup and lazy loading
takeaways.what_they_do: Store container images as metadata pointing to hashed blobs, deduplicating redundant files across images and lazily fetching only accessed data to minimize transfer on cold start.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we store the images the container images as just a bunch of metadata that points to blobs and for each blob we compute a check sum or hash value
takeaways.numbers: cold start reduced below a second

takeaways.technique: CPU memory snapshot/restore for warm starts
takeaways.what_they_do: Snapshot the RAM state of a container after initialization and restore it instead of re-running imports, cutting startup even for large model loads.
takeaways.evidence_quote: what if you can just like revert to the the memory State the CPU memory the ram of of uh a container
takeaways.numbers: stable diffusion starts in a couple of seconds despite 5-10GB weights

takeaways.technique: Usage-based pooling to cut idle capacity
takeaways.what_they_do: Pool many users onto shared dynamic resources so you only pay for active time, improving utilization and lowering cost versus static provisioning.
takeaways.evidence_quote: don't provision more than you actually need just just you know only pay for capacitor you're actually using

takeaways.technique: Fast feedback loop as productivity metric
takeaways.what_they_do: Optimize the iterate-run-observe cycle so code changes execute in the cloud nearly as fast as locally, treating loop latency as the primary productivity lever.
takeaways.evidence_quote: in order to make Engineers fast and make them more productive you want to have this like super fast feedback loop

takeaways.technique: Fan-out parallel execution over many containers
takeaways.what_they_do: Map a function over thousands of inputs, spinning up as many containers as possible to parallelize batch work.
takeaways.evidence_quote: what model does when you fan out is that it's going to spin up as many containers as possible
takeaways.numbers: 18 containers at peak in demo, scaling to thousands
